/**
     * Multiply a float number by a power of 2.

ownership_reason: Only the gold computes the common divisor of the two parts; hop 4 divides both parts by whatever it returns and builds the fraction, hop 2 moves the sign to the numerator, hops 1 and 3 and the facade pass the parts along. With the factors of two left in t, t = (v - u) / 2 halves odd differences and the routine returns a number that does not divide both parts (6 for (6, 8), 3 for (3, 4)); hop 4's exact divisions then truncate, and the value cannot be recovered from the result. The divisor is wrong on reduced inputs too, so no value-preserving change of the parts above the gold (pre-reduction, absolute values, swapped order, sign move) repairs it; only replacing the gold's result (ArithmeticUtils.gcd, or building the fraction from the undivided parts) passes the trigger, which discards the gold. The convention is pinned outside the gold: ArithmeticUtils.gcd(int, int) and gcd(long, long) run the same binary algorithm and cast the factors of two out of t in every pass (ArithmeticUtilsTest testGcd, testGcdLong, testGcdConsistency); Fraction.getReducedFraction reduces both parts by that gcd before building the fraction, and FractionTest testGetReducedFraction asserts getReducedFraction(6, 8) equals 3/4; ArithmeticUtils.lcm divides by the same gcd (testLcm).
